This week, Representative Darren Soto and I introduced the “Federal Investment Restrictions on Equipment from Worrisome Authoritarian Linked Locations (FIREWALL) Act. This bipartisan legislation is designed to safeguard America's telecommunications infrastructure from foreign adversaries by prohibiting federal telecommunications funding from being used to purchase fiber-optic cable sourced from countries of concern. The legislation builds upon ongoing efforts to secure U.S. communications networks from foreign threats and prevent hostile regimes from gaining access to critical American infrastructure. America's telecommunications networks are the backbone of our economy, our national security, and our daily lives. As our adversaries become increasingly sophisticated in their efforts to infiltrate critical infrastructure, we must act proactively to protect our communications systems from potential vulnerabilities. The FIREWALL Actensures that taxpayer dollars are not used to subsidize technology sourced from countries that pose a threat to our national security. Rather than waiting until these products are deeply embedded in our networks and facing another costly 'rip and replace' effort, we should take commonsense steps now to prevent the problem from occurring in the first place.

B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. USDA had approved $378 million in prevention and control funding for sterile fly facilities in 2023 and 2024, yet the money went unspent when the new administration paused funding. This is extremely concerning to our ranchers, and this outbreak could drive the price of food even higher. Unfortunately, we continue to see the fallout of the blunt and ill-considered cuts to federal workers, from the return of New World Screwworm to the United States, to farmers showing up to closed or understaffed Farm Service Agency offices, to attacks on our nuclear safety programs putting national security at risk. I will continue to hold the White House accountable, as I did this week during the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government hearing with Mr. Vought.

Today, Congressman Austin Scott (GA-08) and I testified before the U.S. House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Federal Lands regarding our bipartisan bill, the Ocmulgee Mounds National Park Redesignation Act (H.R. 9416). As our nation prepares to celebrate its 250th birthday this Saturday, it is vital that we preserve and protect our ancient history, including the stories of the indigenous peoples who lived here long before July 4, 1776. Our bill today represents a small, albeit meaningful, step forward that will strengthen Ocmulgee and ensure that its cultural and religious sites are protected now and into the future. Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today. However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process. The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster. I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties. I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities. Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

Today, our nation celebrates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. 250 years ago, our nation overthrew the autocratic rule of King George III, defining our nation’s identity. On Independence Day and every day, I’m grateful for our servicemembers, military families, and veterans who bravely defend our freedom. From the Fundamental Orders of Connecticut, the first written constitution in the colonies, to Governor Jonathan Trumbull’s steadfast support for the Revolutionary cause, our state played an outsized role in the fight for independence. Connecticut earned the nickname “The Provision State” by supplying the Continental Army with food and materials that sustained the fight for freedom. The people of eastern Connecticut were right at the forefront of the Revolution- military leaders such as Major General Israel Putnam of Brooklyn Connecticut, as well as Governor Jonathan Trumbull of Lebanon, the only Colonial Governor to support the rebellion against England. The spirit of service remains part of who we are. Eastern Connecticut continues to strengthen our nation through military service, manufacturing, shipbuilding, agriculture, and so much more. On America’s 250th birthday, we can take pride in the role that our region has played in our nation’s past and continues to play in its future.

On Wednesday, I joined the Southeastern New England Defense Industry Alliance (SENEDIA) in Middletown, RI and Admiral Robert Gaucher, head of U.S. Navy submarine production and repairs, to celebrate a major milestone: 10,000 people have now completed training through our region’s submarine workforce training pipelines. This milestone is more proof that our region, and eastern Connecticut in particular, has risen to the challenge of creating a next-generation submarine workforce.

R to @RepJoeCourtney: In 2015, then-Secretary of Labor Tom Perez joined me for a visit to Electric Boat and a roundtable discussion on manufacturing workforce needs in eastern Connecticut. Following his visit, I worked with the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board (EWIB) to secure a $6 million federal grant from the Department of Labor to kickstart the Manufacturing Pipeline Initiative (MPI). Today, with continued funding from Congress and stalwart support from SENEDIA, the MPI continues to grow and support record hiring numbers at Electric Boat. As of last month, 5,561 metal trades and designer workers have graduated from MPI, and more are coming.

R to @RepJoeCourtney: This 10,000 trained milestone isn’t the end of our work. The historic demand signal from Congress and the Navy for submarine construction requires double the number of skilled shipbuilders. As Ranking Member of the Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee and a member of the Education and Workforce Committee, I will continue working to support workforce training pipelines that keep eastern Connecticut at the forefront of our nation’s defense industrial base.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

On Monday, our office suffered an unimaginable loss. Chris Matthews, my District Outreach and Communications Director, passed away unexpectedly. If any one of you begin to lose faith in our country, remember Chris Matthews. Remember he was without question one of the Commonwealth’s sharpest political minds – a generational talent. Remember that he was more than a Congressional aide. He took the belief that through our actions we all can bring needed change and brought it with him on many interstate bus rides to canvas distant pivotal states and to the doors of the families he inspired. Remember through his example that public service is a genuinely noble vocation. As a trusted member of our office, he helped countless veterans, families, and those who could not advocate for themselves. Those of us privileged to have worked with him for over fifteen years will remember his laugh and his wry, often biting, humor – contrasting the way things are to the way they could be. We will always remember his authentic belief that in this country, people can bring about progress and meaningful change. It was real to him and his sincerity shown through. Chris was a genuinely good person. He was family to all of us, and we are devastated by his loss, particularly at such a young age. Our thoughts and prayers are with Molly and Eli and the many who loved him. Though we wish we had more time with him, his memory will continue to give us faith that one person can significantly make better the lives of those around him.

The Supreme Court’s decision today recognizes that states face unique circumstances in administering their elections. In Alaska, voting is not as simple as driving down the road to a neighborhood polling place. Many Alaskans live in remote communities that are not connected to the road system, requiring ballots to travel by bush plane or boat, which means volatile weather conditions and limited infrastructure can determine whether those ballots arrive on time. Even with Alaska’s current 10-day grace period for in-state ballots, we have seen mail delays cause legally cast ballots to arrive too late to be counted. Today’s decision affirms that states have the flexibility to account for these realities and helps ensure that every American who lawfully casts a ballot has the opportunity to have it counted. https://apnews.com/article/supreme-court-mailed-ballots-trump-elections-5f24f718ea92a33838485ce6302e079e

P000597.text: Only the Trump Administration would spend America's 250th birthday attacking the Smithsonian for telling the truth about American history. It is disgusting, but not surprising, that the White House deliberately timed this 162-page screed for the Fourth of July, when thousands of Americans came to Washington expecting a celebration of our nation’s history. Behind the fireworks and flags, this Administration was quietly launching an authoritarian attack on one of America’s most treasured public institutions, bullying the Smithsonian into whitewashing our past and demanding that history be rewritten to flatter the President and his political movement. Donald Trump is shredding the Constitution. He is corrupting the federal government. He is turning our nation's semiquincentennial into a monument to himself. A president who bulldozed the People's House, tried to hijack the Smithsonian, and wants history rewritten by political loyalists has no business lecturing anyone about love of country. The Smithsonian's job is to tell the full American story: our triumphs and our failures, our progress and our contradictions, the people in power and the people who fought to make this country live up to its promises. The real warning belongs on this report: "Prepared by people who are terrified of honest American history."

No matter our politics, whatever our background or beliefs, today, on America’s 250th birthday, I hope we can all take a moment to reflect on the ideals that have united generations of Americans: freedom, opportunity, a government of, by, and for the people, and a steadfast faith in better days to come. Our country’s story includes extraordinary progress and extraordinary pain. We have a history that cannot and must not be whitewashed, because loving America means telling the truth about where we have fallen short, learning from it, and continuing the hard work of building a nation that lives up to its highest ideals. We are bound to disagree about how best to move forward, and what we owe one another as fellow Americans. But as long as we don’t lose sight of the many things that unite us—this land, the people with whom we share it, and the enduring promise of our democracy—I wholeheartedly believe that we can achieve a more perfect union. We’ve come a long way these past 250 years. Not far or fast enough, perhaps, but a long, world-changing way nonetheless. All of us have a role to play in moving America forward. And *that* is a gift worth celebrating today. Happy 250, America. Here’s to 250 more, and to never giving up on the promise and potential of this extraordinary country—or the people who call it home. 🇺🇸

From the beginning, Trump has treated America 250 like his own personal birthday party. He doesn’t give a shit about honoring our country, let alone helping states and communities put on their own celebrations. All he cares about is putting on a huge, expensive spectacle—and being at the center of the whole thing. Congress needs to take a hard look at how this money was spent, whose pockets are being lined, and why funds appropriated for communities across the country are still being withheld.

Unfortunately, we look to nations outside of our borders to supply us with a resource that we have right here in our own back yard. Healthy forest management is more than just taking care of our trees, in fact we have been loving our trees to death. Our forests are overstocked and unhealthy because we have no markets for the wood and rural communities are suffering because their resource and economic opportunity are tied directly to the forests. A nation with such an abundance of timber should never be reliant on other countries to import lumber and pulp products, but that’s where we find ourselves.  Recently, we’ve seen paper mills across the country closing – even a few here in the Fourth District. With a background in Forestry and Engineering, Congressman Westerman understands just how important our pulp and paper industry is and he remains heavily focused on legislation that will support such an important economic contributer for Arkansas. This week’s meeting with the Pulp & Paperworkers’ Resource Council to discuss just how important the forest products industry underscored the need for Congress to work diligently to provide its support.

S001198.text: During my tenure in the Senate, I have worked to secure historic levels of federal infrastructure investments for Alaska—funding that will help improve roads, bridges, ports, airports, and other crucial projects to our great state. A000375.text: John Adams called Independence Day America’s “Day of Deliverance.” The Declaration of Independence - that sacred parchment - is the cornerstone of American exceptionalism and the foundation for the longest-sustained constitutional democracy in the world. It affirms the birthright of every American citizen: our God-given rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. The Declaration of Independence wasn’t just a list of grievances; it was a treatise on man and his natural rights - a mission statement for how such men should be governed. No one at the time gave us a fighting chance of defeating the world’s superpower for our independence. And few predicted we’d persist for a quarter of a millennium. Our founding visionaries weren’t sure of either outcome themselves, but they believed in our inherent rights and God-given freedoms and would rather die fighting for them than live under tyranny. They trusted in “divine Providence” for protection and mutually pledged to each other “our Lives, our Fortunes and our sacred Honor.” They held fast to truth, they stood firm for justice, and they fought like warrior poets for our freedom. And, by the grace of Almighty God, our revolutionary ancestors gave birth to the most powerful and prosperous nation in human history. Let’s honor their vision, courage, and conviction by solemnly dedicating ourselves to preserving this “Great Experiment” in liberty and self-government. Happy 250th Independence Day to all my God-fearing, freedom-loving American patriots! May God continue to have mercy upon and give favor to our beloved nation. U-S-A, U-S-A…!! Your proud US Representative and fellow West Texan, Jodey

K000377.text: Space Shuttle Endeavour is where it belongs — stacked vertically again, with the external tank and solid rocket boosters and ready for launch. This Independence Day, America marks a special milestone: 250 years as a nation. This country was founded on a few simple principles. Freedom, Democracy, and the idea that all of us are created equal. Those principles have been tested over and over again. From the Revolutionary War to the Civil War and the end of slavery. Through two World Wars, the fight against fascism, the Civil Rights Movement, and beyond. Every generation has worked to make our country better live up to its founding ideals. Our history has never been simple. But what has always made our country exceptional is our willingness to keep pushing forward. We've built the strongest democracy the world has ever known. We've invented, discovered, and explored in ways no other nation has. We learned to fly. We put people on the Moon. We continue to push the boundaries of what's possible because Americans are willing to take on hard problems together. A lot of us were reminded of that earlier this year as we watched Artemis II fly around the Moon and travel farther than any human has ever before. Twenty years ago this Independence Day, I launched on a mission to the International Space Station. As I looked back at Earth, I thought about how unlikely that journey really was. I'm the son of two police officers. I went to public schools. I had the opportunity to become a Navy pilot, an astronaut, and now a United States Senator. In no other place is a path like mine possible. Every generation before us has worked to preserve and strengthen the freedoms we enjoy and leave this country stronger than they found it. It's our turn to do the same. As America celebrates 250 years, we should all be asking ourselves a simple question: What do we want the next 250 years to look like? Do we continue building on the values that have carried us this far: Freedom, democracy, and equality? Do we keep investing in the next generation of innovators, explorers, workers, and public servants? Do we keep choosing unity over division and solve problems together? I think the choice is simple. Those before us sacrificed to build this country and protect our democracy. Now it's our responsibility to strengthen it for our kids and grandkids. If we stay committed to those ideals and do the work to preserve them, then I have no doubt the next 250 years can be even better than the last. Today we celebrate our freedoms. Tomorrow we get to work preserving them. Happy Fourth of July.

RT by @RepBlakeMoore: Dear America,   Starting today, on the 250th birthday of our country, millions of children will now benefit from a new & powerful American birthright - a privately owned investment account from birth. Every child a shareholder in the great American economy! American capitalism is the greatest prosperity-creating engine the world has ever known. It has unlocked unprecedented abundance for our country and untold life-advancing innovation. From clean food & water to cars & planes to vaccines & cures to computers & phones.  Through depressions & world wars, through panics & pandemics, betting on America has been the best investment in human history.  But far too many hardworking families feel like they are on the outside looking in - like the American Dream has become out of reach.  The Invest America Act changes all that. Signed into law by President Trump it establishes the Trump Accounts - launching today - making every child a shareholder from birth.  Every account seeded with $1000 in America's best companies - making every child a direct participant in our stock markets & American capitalism.   But it doesn’t stop there.  Representing the best of our civic traditions, an unprecedented outpouring of additional private  contributions into these accounts is already underway. Billions of dollars have been committed by philanthropists & corporations to tens of millions of children across the country. A new form of massive, direct philanthropy & corporate benefits directly to America’s kids is just getting started. From adopting all the kids of a school or organization to a city or state.  America is the most giving country in the history of the world - and Trump Accounts provide a new open source platform to enable anybody to contribute to anybody.   Trillions of dollars will compound in these accounts over the next 20 years.    But this is about more than just figures on an account statement. By investing in the next generation, our country is providing tangible opportunities to all future generations of Americans: an education, a first home, the ability to start a business, and the foundation for a lifetime of savings. Trump Accounts provide hope to those feeling hopeless - unlocking unlimited human potential. Trump Accounts do this through a massive public - private partnership that empower the individual not the state.  They double down on free market capitalist democracy by empowering the individual rather than growing dependency on government.  Aligning citizens with capitalism rather than pitting them against it.  Perhaps of equal importance, let us not lose sight of the fact that this is a movement that unites our country. Despite the many issues that divide us, this one big idea brings everyone together. From the most conservative to the most progressive leaders, we have found people of goodwill willing to step up and do the right thing to help the next generation.  Trump Accounts represent the very best of our democracy and the American promise issued two hundred and fifty years ago today. I am grateful to all those who have partnered with us to get this far and we dedicate our tireless efforts to make certain that the Invest America Act achieves its maximum potential.  Let us advance into the future with a renewed sense of confidence, optimism and restored faith in the American Dream for EVERY American.    Happy 250th Birthday, America! On this day in 1785, the Continental Congress established the dollar as the official currency of the United States. Before and during the American Revolution, Congress issued paper money known as “Continentals,” but rampant inflation quickly rendered it nearly worthless. In creating a national currency, Congress based the U.S. dollar on the widely circulated Spanish silver dollar, even adopting the familiar “$” symbol derived from the Spanish-American peso. Today, the U.S. dollar is the world’s primary reserve currency and one of the most widely used and trusted currencies in global commerce.

L000603.text: One year ago today, on the Fourth of July, our nation celebrated the blessings of freedom while families across Texas experienced unimaginable heartbreak. We pause today to remember every precious life lost at Camp Mystic and every other life taken far too soon in that tragedy. We remember the children whose futures were just beginning, the counselors and adults who stood courageously in harm’s way, and every family whose lives were forever changed. Their names, their stories, and their memories will never be forgotten. No words can truly ease the pain of such profound loss. Yet even in the darkest moments, we witnessed the very best of America. To every law enforcement officer, firefighter, EMS professional, dispatcher, game warden, pilot, medic, search-and-rescue specialist, and every first responder who answered the call, thank you. You ran toward danger while others were running away. You worked through exhaustion, heartbreak, and impossible conditions with courage, professionalism, and compassion. Your service honored every life you were fighting to save. To the countless volunteers who showed up without being asked—neighbors, veterans, church groups, ranchers, boat owners, businesses, families, and complete strangers—you reminded us that the strength of our communities is measured not only by what we say, but by what we do. You brought supplies, comfort, equipment, prayers, and hope. You asked for nothing in return except the opportunity to help another human being. That spirit defines Texas. As we remember those we lost, let us also remember the enduring responsibility we share: to love our neighbors, to care for those who grieve, and to ensure that the memories of these lives continue to inspire acts of kindness, service, and sacrifice. Finally, I want to offer my deepest gratitude to the men of the BEARKAT team. There are simply no words sufficient to express what you endured or what you accomplished. You answered a calling that demanded extraordinary courage, unwavering resolve, and selfless service. You carried burdens that few will ever fully understand, and you did so with quiet professionalism and humility. It is impossible to thank you enough for all that you did. Your actions brought comfort to grieving families, hope in moments of despair, and honor to everyone you represent. Texas will forever be grateful, and your service will never be forgotten. May we always remember those we lost, honor those who served, and carry forward the enduring truth that even in our darkest hours, courage, compassion, and faith will always light the way.
Happy Fourth of July, America. God bless 🇺🇸
250 years of American freedom, strength, and prosperity 🇺🇸

What to Know About Congresswoman King-Hinds’ Co-Sponsored Bill Our office is committed to keeping our community informed about the legislation being introduced in Congress that could impact the Marianas. The Territorial Small Business Development Act of 2026, co-sponsored by Congresswoman King-Hinds, would establish a new SBA program to support eligible small businesses in the CNMI, Guam, and American Samoa. The Supreme Court has now issued its decision on birthright citizenship, resolving one of the most significant constitutional cases before the Court this term. The ruling reaffirms that the 14th Amendment guarantees U.S. citizenship to individuals born in the United States, regardless of their parents’ immigration status, and confirms that the longstanding 1898 Wong Kim Ark decision remains the law of the land. In this update, I wanted to take a few minutes to walk through what the Court decided, why the executive order restricting birthright citizenship cannot be enforced, and what the ruling means from a constitutional perspective. I hope this provides a straightforward overview of the decision and its broader legal significance.

As of Monday morning, several thousand residents of the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos continue to lack power. Here’s what you need to know: ⚡ Avoid downed power lines. If you live in PPL’s service area and encounter a downed line, please call 1-800-342-5775 and say "downed power line." 📅 Know the schedule. While most local residents have had their power restored, some of those impacted by more complex outages remain without power. PPL anticipates that power will be restored to all areas by Wednesday, July 8th, with many seeing earlier restorations. ℹ️ Stay informed. Get updates, report outages, and see the latest map by visiting https://stories.pplelectric.com/storm-updates/ 💵 Keep receipts for ice and gallons of water. PPL is offering reimbursement for up to three 10lb bags of ice and three gallons of water per day for those impacted. Thank you to the local lineworkers who are working around the clock to restore power to our community.

La France a déployé au Moyen-Orient des moyens de déminage, avec notamment deux chasseurs de mines. Accompagnés de deux frégates et d’un avion de patrouille maritime, ces moyens sont prêts à contribuer, avec nos partenaires, à la pleine reprise de la navigation et à garantir la sécurité du trafic dans le détroit d’Ormuz. La signature, le 17 juin dernier, du mémorandum d’accord entre les États-Unis et l’Iran constitue une avancée importante en faveur de la stabilité régionale, en réaffirmant notamment la liberté de navigation dans le détroit d’Ormuz. Compte tenu de cette évolution favorable et de l’évolution des besoins, à l’issue des échanges constructifs que j’ai eus avec le Sultan d’Oman, j’ai décidé d’adapter notre dispositif. Le porte-avions Charles de Gaulle rejoint ainsi son port d’attache à Toulon, tandis que nos moyens de déminage et leur escorte demeurent déployés et prêts à intervenir avec nos partenaires. La France reste pleinement mobilisée et continuera d’ajuster ses moyens en fonction de l’évolution de la situation et des besoins de sécurité dans la région.
